note: WAEC Literature round 5 (R27 top-up): personification (garden smiled), hyperbole (thousand times), euphemism (passed on), metonymy (pen and sword), synecdoche (all hands), oxymoron (deafening silence), paradox (child father of man), pun (grave man), litotes (not bad), apostrophe (O Milton); soliloquy, dramatic irony (Othello-Iago), denouement, catharsis, chorus, tragedy, protagonist; elegy, ode, sonnet 14 lines, ballad, dirge, oriki, refrain, couplet; omniscient narrator, setting, flat character, motif, flashback, theme; riddle, folktale, myth, call-and-response; The Concubine (Amadi), Purple Hibiscus (Adichie), Song of Lawino (p'Bitek), The Lion and the Jewel (Soyinka), The African Child (Laye). Scanned against WAEC rounds 1-4, NECO Literature (all rounds) and the JAMB pool.
